rows.stem: An ecosystem contains maximum number of :
rows.solution:
Producers (green plants) form the first trophic level and the base of every food chain. Only about 10% of the energy at one level passes on to the next, so each higher level can support fewer organisms. The producers are therefore present in the largest number.

This is option (A) Producers.

rows.stem: Select the incorrect statement from the following :

options.label: A
options.text: Ozone is a molecule formed by three atoms of oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: Ozone shields earth’s surface from harmful infrared radiations.

options.label: C
options.text: CFC’s are linked to decline of \(\mathrm{O_3}\) layer in our atmosphere.

options.label: D
options.text: Ozone at higher levels is a product of UV radiations acting on oxygen molecule.

rows.solution:
Ozone is \(\mathrm{O_3}\), a molecule of three oxygen atoms, so the first statement is correct. At higher levels of the atmosphere it is formed when ultraviolet radiation splits oxygen molecules into free oxygen atoms, which combine with oxygen molecules:

\(\mathrm{O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} O + O}\) and \(\mathrm{O + O_2 \rightarrow O_3}\)

CFCs are linked to the decline of the ozone layer. But the ozone layer shields the earth's surface from harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun, not from infrared radiation, so that statement is the incorrect one.

This is option (B) Ozone shields earth’s surface from harmful infrared radiations.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** In case of iodine deficiency in our diet, there is a possibility that we might suffer from goitre.

**Reason (R) :** One of the symptoms of goitre is swelling of neck.
rows.context: Question No. 8 & 9 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to make the hormone thyroxin. If the diet lacks iodine, we may suffer from goitre, so the Assertion is true. Goitre does show itself as a swollen neck, so the Reason is also true. But a symptom of goitre does not explain why iodine deficiency causes it; the explanation is that iodine is needed to make thyroxin.

Both are true, but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (B).

rows.stem: Why the lungs always contain a residual volume of air ?
rows.solution: During breathing, air is taken in and let out of the lungs, but the lungs are never emptied completely. They always contain a residual volume of air so that there is sufficient time for oxygen to be absorbed into the blood and for carbon dioxide to be released from it. This keeps gas exchange going continuously, even between breaths.

rows.stem:
(a) Show a cross between a pea plant having round & green seed with a pea plant having wrinkled and yellow seeds upto \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation.

(b) Also write down results of \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation.
rows.solution:
(a) Parents: round green (RRyy) \(\times\) wrinkled yellow (rrYY). Their gametes are Ry and rY, so every \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plant is RrYy, with round yellow seeds.

The \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are self-pollinated. Each forms four kinds of gametes, RY, Ry, rY and ry, in equal numbers, giving the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation:

| | RY | Ry | rY | ry |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RY | RRYY | RRYy | RrYY | RrYy |
| Ry | RRYy | RRyy | RrYy | Rryy |
| rY | RrYY | RrYy | rrYY | rrYy |
| ry | RrYy | Rryy | rrYy | rryy |

(b) Results of the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation, out of 16:

Round, yellow: 9

Round, green: 3

Wrinkled, yellow: 3

Wrinkled, green: 1

The phenotypic ratio is 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. Two new combinations, round yellow and wrinkled green, appear that were not present in the parents, showing that the two traits are inherited independently.

rows.stem:
Magnesium ribbon burns with a dazzling white flame and changes into a white powder as shown in the diagram given below :

The powder is dissolved in water.

Identify the chemical formula of the white powder and the correct change observed when the solution is tested with litmus paper.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - a drawing of the burning-magnesium activity: a hand holds a magnesium ribbon in tongs in a burner flame above a watch-glass on a wooden board, with labels 'Tong', 'Magnesium ribbon', 'Burner', 'Watch-glass' and 'Magnesium oxide' (the white powder in the watch-glass). The stem states everything the question needs; note the drawing's own label names the product. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
Magnesium burns in air to form magnesium oxide, the white powder:

\(\mathrm{2Mg(s) + O_2(g) \rightarrow 2MgO(s)}\)

Magnesium oxide is a basic oxide. It dissolves in water to form magnesium hydroxide, a base:

\(\mathrm{MgO(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow Mg(OH)_2(aq)}\)

A basic solution turns red litmus blue. The formula is MgO, since magnesium has valency 2 and oxygen has valency 2.

This is option (B) \(\mathrm{MgO}\), turns red litmus blue.

rows.stem:
Galvanization is a process of coating iron articles with a thin layer of zinc to prevent iron from rusting. The iron is protected even if the zinc coating is scratched and iron is exposed. Which of the following is/are true about how zinc prevents the rusting of iron ?

(P) A galvanised iron article does not undergo oxidation.

(Q) The zinc coating prevents contact of iron with air.

(R) Zinc provides continuous protection to iron from rusting.
rows.solution:
Statement (P) is false: zinc itself is oxidised (it is more reactive than iron), so a galvanised article does undergo oxidation; it is the zinc that is oxidised rather than the iron.

Statement (Q) is true: the zinc coating keeps air and moisture away from the iron.

Statement (R) is true: zinc is more reactive than iron, so even where the coating is scratched and the iron is exposed, zinc is oxidised in preference to iron. The protection continues as long as zinc remains.

This is option (C) (Q) and (R).

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: Write the preparation of Baking soda. How does it help in making cakes soft and spongy ?
rows.solution:
Baking soda (sodium hydrogencarbonate) is prepared by passing carbon dioxide and ammonia through a cold aqueous solution of sodium chloride (brine):

\(\mathrm{NaCl + H_2O + CO_2 + NH_3 \rightarrow NH_4Cl + NaHCO_3}\)

On heating during baking, baking soda decomposes and releases carbon dioxide gas:

\(\mathrm{2NaHCO_3 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Na_2CO_3 + H_2O + CO_2}\)

The bubbles of carbon dioxide make the dough rise, so the cake becomes soft and spongy. (In baking powder, baking soda is mixed with a mild edible acid such as tartaric acid, which also produces carbon dioxide and neutralises the sodium carbonate that would otherwise give a bitter taste.)

rows.stem:
What happens when

(i) potassium iodide solution is added to lead (II) nitrate solution ?

(ii) zinc is added to copper (II) chloride solution ?

(iii) hydrogen gas is passed over hot copper (II) oxide ?

Write balanced chemical equations of the reactions involved in support of your answer.
rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: says a yellow precipitate of potassium iodide is formed in (i); the yellow precipitate is lead(II) iodide, \(\mathrm{PbI_2}\), as the scheme's own equation shows, and potassium nitrate stays in solution.]

(i) A yellow precipitate of lead(II) iodide is formed. This is a double displacement (precipitation) reaction.

\(\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2(aq) + 2KI(aq) \rightarrow PbI_2(s) + 2KNO_3(aq)}\)

(ii) Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper(II) chloride solution. The blue colour of the solution fades and reddish brown copper is deposited.

\(\mathrm{Zn(s) + CuCl_2(aq) \rightarrow ZnCl_2(aq) + Cu(s)}\)

(iii) Hydrogen reduces copper(II) oxide to copper, so the black copper oxide turns reddish brown, and water is formed.

\(\mathrm{CuO(s) + H_2(g) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Cu(s) + H_2O(l)}\)

rows.stem:
When an incident ray of light enters in a medium ‘X’ from medium ‘Y’, it bends away from the normal.

Comment about the following :

(a) Speed of light in medium ‘X’ with respect to the speed of light in medium of ‘Y’.

(b) Optical density of medium ‘X’ with respect to the optical density of medium ‘Y’.

Give reason for your answer in each case.
rows.solution:
A ray going from an optically denser medium into an optically rarer medium bends away from the normal. Here the ray bends away from the normal on entering X from Y, so X is the rarer medium.

(a) The speed of light in X is more than in Y, because light travels faster in an optically rarer medium, and a ray bends away from the normal when it speeds up.

(b) The optical density of X is less than that of Y, because a ray bends away from the normal only when it passes into an optically rarer medium.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem:
An object of height 6 cm is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the optical centre of a concave lens of focal length 15 cm.

Use lens formula to determine :

(a) The distance of image from the optical centre.

(b) The height of the image formed.
rows.solution:
For a concave lens, \(h = 6\) cm, \(u = -30\) cm and \(f = -15\) cm.

(a) By the lens formula:

\(\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}\), so \(\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{-15} + \frac{1}{-30} = \frac{-2 - 1}{30} = -\frac{1}{10}\)

\(v = -10\) cm. The image is formed 10 cm from the optical centre, on the same side as the object.

(b) Magnification: \(m = \frac{v}{u} = \frac{-10}{-30} = \frac{1}{3}\).

Since \(m = \frac{h'}{h}\), the height of the image is \(h' = m \times h = \frac{1}{3} \times 6 = 2\) cm.

The image is 2 cm high; the positive sign shows it is virtual and erect.

rows.stem:
(i) State the rule which gives the direction of force acting on a current carrying conductor placed in a uniform magnetic field.

(ii) Name any two devices which work on the basis of an interaction between magnetic field and current carrying conductor.

(iii) Observe the given diagrams :

Comment on the magnitude of force on electron in both the cases and give reason for your answer.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - part (iii) refers to two printed diagrams, labelled (I) and (II). Each shows five parallel horizontal arrows labelled 'Magnetic Field' and an electron 'e' with an arrow labelled 'Movement of electron'. The direction of the electron's motion relative to the field in each panel is withheld because it is what (iii) tests. Page idx 30.
rows.solution:
(i) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of motion of, or the force acting on, the conductor.

(ii) Any two: electric motor, loudspeaker, measuring instruments such as the galvanometer and ammeter.

(iii) In diagram (I) the electron moves at right angles to the magnetic field, so the force on it is maximum. The force on a moving charge (like that on a current-carrying conductor) is greatest when the motion is perpendicular to the field.

In diagram (II) the electron moves along the direction of the magnetic field, so the force on it is zero. A charge moving parallel (or antiparallel) to the field experiences no force.

rows.stem:
(i) List three possible reasons of short-circuiting in an electric circuit.

(ii) In case of overload, will the fuse protect to given electric circuit from damage ? Justify your answer.

(iii) For an electric heater rated as 220 V, 2200 W, what should be the minimum rating of fuse used with it ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - part (ii) is a printed circuit drawing with no words of its own in the stem: an 'Electric heater' (a box with a coil) connected by two wires to a '220 V AC supply', the wires labelled 'Live wire' and 'Neutral wire', with a 'Fuse' drawn in one of them. Which wire carries the fuse is withheld because it is what (ii) tests. Page idx 30.
rows.solution:
(i) Any three:

1. The live wire and the neutral wire come into direct contact.

2. The insulation of the wires is damaged, worn out or torn (for example in old wiring), which lets the bare wires touch.

3. Overloading, which overheats the wires and can melt their insulation, so that the live and neutral wires touch.

4. A fault inside an appliance, or loose connections.

(ii) No. In the given circuit the fuse is connected in the neutral wire. On overload the fuse may blow, but the heater stays connected to the live wire, so it remains at 220 V and anyone touching it can still get a shock; a leakage from the live wire to earth would not pass through the fuse at all. To protect the circuit, the fuse must be connected in series with the live wire.

(iii) The current drawn by the heater is

\(I = \frac{P}{V} = \frac{2200\,\mathrm{W}}{220\,\mathrm{V}} = 10\) A

So the fuse must be rated slightly more than 10 A (in practice a fuse of the next standard rating above 10 A is used); a fuse rated below 10 A would blow during normal use.
